terms.label: 11 personnel
terms.definition: One running back, one tight end, and three wide receivers on offense.

terms.label: shotgun
terms.definition: Quarterback aligned several yards behind the center at the snap.

terms.label: four verticals
terms.definition: A vertical distribution concept with four eligible threats stressing deep coverage lanes.

terms.label: Cover 3
terms.definition: A three-deep coverage structure with underneath defenders allocated by the call.

terms.label: odd front
terms.definition: A defensive front family organized around an odd-technique interior structure.

terms.label: inside zone
terms.definition: A zone run concept in which the line works combination blocks and the runner presses an interior track before making a read.

terms.label: red zone
terms.definition: The field area from the opponent 20-yard line to the goal line.

terms.label: third down
terms.definition: A down in which the offense normally seeks the line to gain before fourth down.

terms.label: quarterback
terms.definition: The offensive player responsible for receiving the snap and executing the play’s quarterback assignment.

terms.label: center
terms.definition: The interior offensive lineman who normally initiates the snap.

terms.label: running back
terms.definition: An offensive back responsible for carrying, receiving, protection, or route execution according to the play design.

terms.label: wide receiver
terms.definition: An eligible offensive receiver responsible for route execution, leverage, spacing, and blocking assignments.

terms.label: tight end
terms.definition: An eligible offensive player aligned in a tight or detached position with receiving and blocking responsibilities.

terms.label: offensive tackle
terms.definition: An offensive lineman aligned at the edge of the offensive line and responsible for protection or run-blocking assignments.

terms.label: defensive end
terms.definition: A defensive front player aligned at or near the edge with rush, set-edge, or contain responsibilities.

terms.label: defensive tackle
terms.definition: An interior defensive lineman responsible for controlling gaps, disrupting blocks, or rushing the passer.

terms.label: linebacker
terms.definition: A second-level defender responsible for run fits, coverage, pressure, or communication assignments.

terms.label: cornerback
terms.definition: A defensive back responsible for coverage, leverage, support, or pressure according to the call.

terms.label: safety
terms.definition: A deep or hybrid defensive back responsible for coverage structure, run support, communication, or disguise.

terms.label: 10 personnel
terms.definition: One running back and four wide receivers on offense.

terms.label: 12 personnel
terms.definition: One running back, two tight ends, and two wide receivers on offense.

terms.label: pistol
terms.definition: A formation with the quarterback aligned several yards behind the center and the back aligned directly behind the quarterback.

terms.label: under center
terms.definition: A formation in which the quarterback receives the snap directly from the center.

terms.label: mesh
terms.definition: A crossing-route concept designed to create traffic and leverage against underneath coverage.

terms.label: boot
terms.definition: A play-action or movement-pass concept that changes the quarterback launch point and stresses the edge and flat defender.

terms.label: outside zone
terms.definition: A zone run concept that presses the edge while the offensive line works lateral tracks and combination blocks.

terms.label: power
terms.definition: A gap-scheme run using a designated puller and a lead-blocking structure to create a defined entry point.

terms.label: Cover 1
terms.definition: A one-high coverage structure commonly pairing a post safety with man or match responsibilities underneath.

terms.label: Cover 2
terms.definition: A two-deep coverage structure dividing the deep field while underneath defenders support the call.

terms.label: quarters
terms.definition: A four-deep-match family in which safeties and cornerbacks distribute vertical threats by read rules.

terms.label: even front
terms.definition: A defensive front family organized around an even-technique interior structure.

terms.label: over front
terms.definition: An even-front alignment that shifts the three-technique and front strength relative to the offensive formation.

terms.label: under front
terms.definition: A front alignment that shifts the defensive line and linebacker structure away from the offensive strength call.

terms.label: all-out pressure
terms.definition: A pressure call that sends more rushers than the protection can naturally account for and requires defined coverage replacement.

terms.label: simulated pressure
terms.definition: A pressure presentation that changes the rushers and coverage picture while typically maintaining a four-man rush count.

terms.label: kickoff
terms.definition: A free kick used to begin a half or restart play after a score, with defined coverage and return responsibilities.

terms.label: punt
terms.definition: A scrimmage kick used to change field position, with operation, protection, coverage, and return decisions.

terms.label: field goal
terms.definition: A place kick attempt requiring snap, hold, protection, operation, and block-response responsibilities.

terms.label: two-minute
terms.definition: A late-half or late-game clock context in which timeouts, clock rules, sequencing, and risk tolerance affect decisions.

terms.label: short yardage
terms.definition: A down-and-distance context requiring a short gain to sustain the drive or convert.

terms.label: dual-threat quarterback
terms.definition: A quarterback whose credible run ability materially changes defensive numbers, fits, and coverage responses.

terms.label: reduced split
terms.definition: A receiver alignment tighter to the core than a standard split, changing access, leverage, and blocking geometry.

terms.label: jet motion
terms.definition: A fast lateral motion across or toward the formation used to influence support, leverage, or the snap picture.

terms.label: gap blocking
terms.definition: A blocking family in which the scheme creates a defined entry point through down blocks, pulls, and leverage blocks.

terms.label: slant
terms.definition: An inside-breaking route that attacks leverage and usually enters a defined interior window at controlled depth.

terms.label: half-slide protection
terms.definition: A pass-protection structure combining a sliding side with man or gap responsibilities on the opposite side.

terms.label: play-action keeper
terms.definition: A play-action design in which the quarterback carries out a run influence and keeps the ball to attack a changed edge or coverage relation.

terms.label: tunnel screen
terms.definition: A screen in which the receiver catches behind coordinated perimeter blocks and works inside a designed blocking tunnel.

terms.label: glance RPO
terms.definition: A run-pass option pairing a run action with a quick inside-breaking glance route keyed to a conflict defender.

terms.label: carry rule
terms.definition: A coverage match instruction to carry an eligible threat vertically or through a defined exchange point before passing it to another defender.

terms.label: spill fit
terms.definition: A run-fit technique that forces the ball wider or to an unblocked support player by controlling the inside shoulder or gap.

terms.label: top of the numbers
terms.definition: The field landmark at the upper edge of the numbers used to describe alignment, route location, and spacing.

terms.label: conflict defender
terms.definition: A defender whose assignment is stressed by two simultaneous threats and whose movement determines the quarterback or ball-carrier decision.

terms.label: alert
terms.definition: A pre-snap or post-snap instruction that changes the call, protection, route, or assignment when a specified trigger is identified.
